questions.q: What command compiles every model, test, and description into a browsable documentation site?
options: dbt docs generate
dbt run --docs
dbt build --site
dbt test --generate-docs
questions.explain: dbt docs generate introspects the whole project — models, sources, tests, snapshots, and live warehouse column metadata — into a static site.

questions.q: What two things does the generated dbt docs site actually contain, according to this lesson?
options: A searchable catalog of every resource with column-level metadata, and an interactive lineage graph generated from ref() calls
A billing dashboard and a user-permissions manager
A raw text dump of every .sql file with no navigation
A list of every Slack message mentioning the project
questions.explain: The catalog surfaces schema.yml descriptions and tests per resource, while the lineage graph is the project-wide, clickable version of the DAG concept from Lesson 1.

questions.q: How do you set up dbt docs to regenerate automatically instead of manually every time?
options: Turn on 'Generate docs on run' in a dbt Cloud job's execution settings, then point the project's Artifacts setting at that job
It is automatic by default and cannot be configured
By adding a cron job that runs `dbt docs generate` outside of dbt entirely, with no dbt Cloud support
By manually re-uploading the site's HTML files after every change
questions.explain: This is the real, documented dbt Cloud workflow: enable docs generation on a job, then wire that job to the project's Artifacts setting.

questions.q: What does it mean that dbt docs 'always show the last fully successful run'?
options: If a job fails partway through, the docs site keeps showing whatever the previous successful run produced, not a blank or broken state
The docs site is deleted and rebuilt from scratch after every single run, successful or not
Docs only update once per calendar month regardless of how often jobs run
A failed run immediately shows an error page instead of any documentation
questions.explain: This is a deliberate design choice — nobody wants documentation reflecting a broken build, so the site freezes at the last green run instead.

questions.q: What practical risk does the 'last successful run' behavior create, according to this lesson?
options: A docs site can be technically accurate and still describe yesterday's code if today's run hasn't gone green yet
It causes dbt test to silently skip failing tests
It means the lineage graph can never be trusted at all
It prevents any model from ever being documented
questions.explain: Trusting a docs site during a red pipeline means you might be looking at a description of code that's since changed, until a new run succeeds.
